A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiAnimate work, with readable text, mathematical definitions, figures and tables. All supplied pages were inspected; neither PDF contains an appendix, and both end with references.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–2 and qualitative experiments and ablations in Figures 6–10.

after.justification: Section 4 retains these original empirical results, including multi-character animation comparisons, TikTok evaluation and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same reference and motion streams, Identifier Assigner, Identifier Adapter and randomized identifier training strategy. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both use Swing Dance, Gen-dataset, TikTok and unseen dance videos featuring 3–7 characters. The revised Table 1 caption matches the existing dataset description; it does not establish changed coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MimicMotion, DisPose, UniAnimate-DiT and VACE. Table 2 retains DisPose and UniAnimate-DiT, with no added or removed comparator.

E3.justification: Dataset split descriptions, six evaluation metrics and training settings are unchanged. Stage 1, Stage 2 and Extended models retain their respective 7,000, 2,400 and 4,200 training steps.

E4.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the same Gen-dataset training comparison, addition-driven versus mask-driven analysis, Identifier Assigner/Adapter ablation and single-person compatibility checks.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, the proposed method's unseen-dance PSNR/FVD remain 23.24/358.74, and its TikTok PSNR remains 23.68.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of inputs, masks and label representations, together with the identifier-bank reasoning in Section 3, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty, identity-consistency, generalization beyond two-character training and single-person compatibility claims.

C2.justification: Explanations of pose ambiguity, channel-identity binding and mask-based generalization are unchanged. Both retain the qualification that the Gen-dataset LPIPS and FID-VID results suggest weaker adaptation to diverse environments.

D1.justification: Section 4 retains the same pose/mask extraction tools, pretrained initialization, hardware, batch size and learning rate. The video-demo access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds background citations to dparallel, Relational Diffusion Distillation, Q-VDiT and SparseD, with corresponding bibliography entries. Existing works and the paper's substantive novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Section 2 lightly trims wording, including 'UNet backbone' to 'UNet' and 'DiT-based video diffusion frameworks' to 'DiT-based frameworks.' Section order and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1's caption changes 'Unseen three-person videos' to 'Unseen dance videos.' Figures and table structures remain unchanged; limited text and bibliography reflow carries the final references onto another page.

improvement.justification: The revised Table 1 caption agrees with its row label and Section 4's existing description of 3–7-character videos, resolving a small reporting inconsistency. This modestly improves clarity; the added citations and wording edits leave the method, empirical evidence and reproducibility information unchanged.
